advances: The weighted preservation obstruction in an actual mixed lattice product at its integer-base centroid.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
At first coordinate $q\in[-1,1]$, the coefficients of the two endpoint cubes in a convex combination are $(1+q)/2$ and $(1-q)/2$. The resulting section is exactly $[(q-1)/2,(q+1)/2]^{n-1}$. In particular $P_n$ is full-dimensional and centrally symmetric about zero. Integer first coordinates can only be $-1,0,1$. At either endpoint the section contributes its $2^{n-1}$ integer cube vertices, and at zero only the origin is integral. Every corresponding fiber is exactly $T$. With the sum of planar areas on these fibers as measure, equal areas give uniform base weights and independent uniform triangle coordinates. The origin is the counting centroid of the bases by symmetry, and the continuous centroid is $(1/3,1/3)$.

At the two outer layers, their equal weights give the same average law as adding equiprobable noise $\pm1/6$ to the centered triangle height. Its score has signed gap $-\lambda/18$ by the symmetric-noise counterexample. The origin layer gives the unperturbed tails $(5/9,0,1)$ by the same triangle formula and hence has signed gap $1/9$. The weights of the combined outer layers and origin layer are $2m/(2m+1)$ and $1/(2m+1)$, so the total gap is $(1-m\lambda)/[9(2m+1)]$. In particular any power of two $m>1/\lambda$ gives a violation. For $m=2$, averaging the tail triples gives $(7/15,0,43/45)$, and at $\lambda=7/9$ the score is $98/81$ against $11/9$. The linear functional has a nonzero integer-base coefficient and a nonzero continuous coefficient, so its cut boundaries are mixed-null in each fiber.
statement:
For every integer $n\ge2$, set
$$
P_n=\operatorname{conv}\left((\{1\}\times[0,1]^{n-1})\cup(\{-1\}\times[-1,0]^{n-1})\right),\qquad
m=2^{n-1},\qquad T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2).
$$
The actual product $P_n\times T$ has $m$ positive-area integer fibers in each endpoint layer and one at the origin, all equal to $T$, and its mixed centroid is $(0,1/3,1/3)$. For its normalized mixed law put $G(v)=\Pr((X_1+X_2)/2-1/3+z_1/6\ge v)$. Then at $s=1/3$ the signed gap $G(0)+G(s)+\lambda G(-s)-(4/9+\lambda)$ is $(1-m\lambda)/[9(2m+1)]$. For each $\lambda>0$ some $n$ gives a strict deficit. At $n=2,\lambda=7/9$, the tails are $(7/15,0,43/45)$ and the deficit is $1/81$.
title: An actual centrally symmetric lattice product violates weighted-tail preservation
